title: Symmetry
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Symmetry. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Line symmetry

A line of symmetry divides a figure into two congruent mirror images. Corresponding points lie equal perpendicular distances from the line. A figure may have zero, one or several lines of symmetry.

Rotational symmetry

A figure has rotational symmetry when a turn smaller than a full turn maps it onto itself. Its order is the number of matching positions in one 360-degree turn; the smallest positive angle is (\(360/order\)) degrees.

Coordinate reflections

Reflection across the x-axis maps ((\(x,y\))) to ((x,-y)); across the y-axis it maps to ((-x,y)); across the origin it maps to ((-x,-y)). A reflection preserves lengths and angles but reverses orientation.

Worked example: A regular hexagon has six reflection axes and rotational symmetry of order 6. Its smallest matching turn is (\(360/6=60\)) degrees.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• For line symmetry, test whether folding on the proposed line makes every point coincide.
  • Count distinct matching positions during one complete 360-degree turn.
  • Do not count the full 360-degree turn as an additional nontrivial position.
  • Use coordinate rules to track signs under reflection.
  • Translation slides a figure and does not create a mirror image or turn.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Reflection preserves distances and angle sizes.
  • Order 1 means no nontrivial rotational symmetry.
  • A circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry through every angle.
  • A non-square rectangle has two lines of symmetry and rotational order 2.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    What is the rotational symmetry order of a square?

    1. (\(1\))
    2. (\(2\))
    3. (\(3\))
    4. (\(4\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(4\))

    The square matches itself at (\(90^\circ,180^\circ,270^\circ\)), and (\(360^\circ\)), giving order 4.

  2. Core:

    How many lines of reflection symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?

    1. (\(1\))
    2. (\(2\))
    3. (\(3\))
    4. (\(6\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3\))

    Each vertex-to-opposite-side midpoint line is a reflection axis. There are three vertices, so there are 3 lines.

  3. Foundation:

    How many lines of symmetry does a non-square rectangle have?

    1. (\(1\))
    2. (\(2\))
    3. (\(3\))
    4. (\(4\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(2\))

    A non-square rectangle has one horizontal and one vertical midpoint axis, so it has 2.

  4. Standard:

    A regular pentagon has rotational symmetry of what order?

    1. (\(2\))
    2. (\(4\))
    3. (\(5\))
    4. (\(10\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(5\))

    A regular n-sided polygon maps to itself n times in one full turn. For a pentagon the order is 5.

  5. Challenge:

    Reflect the point (\((-3,4)\)) across the y-axis. What is its image?

    1. (\((-3,-4)\))
    2. (\((3,4)\))
    3. (\((3,-4)\))
    4. (\((4,-3)\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\((3,4)\))

    Reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of x and keeps y: (\((-3,4)\)) maps to (\((3,4)\)).
